text.p: - Final unofficial results of Sunday's general election would give the ruling Liberal Democrats 25 seats in the new 90-seat parliament, the People's Party 18, and the Social Democrats 16 seats.
- Slovenia signed a temporary agreement with the European Union on Monday to improve trade ties from next year following last June's signing of an associate agreement with the bloc.
- A new round of talks between the succesor republics of the former Yugoslavia is to start in Brussels on Tuesday.
- A delegation of the Netherland's Royal Airforce visited Slovenia on Monday to promote their F-16 fighter aircraft.
- More than 1,600 pilgrims from Slovenia are expected to join a pilgrimage to the Vatican next month to thank the Pope for his visit to Slovenia last May.

- Lojze Peterle, the head of the Christian Democrats, offered his resignation on Monday because of the bad result his party scored in Sunday's election. The party is expected to hold 10 seats in the next parliament, down from 16 currently.
- Slovenia's outgoing parliament convened for the last time on Monday, one day after elections to determine the composition of the next legislature.

- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek of the ruling Liberal Democrats said the "Spring Alliance" of rightwing parties parties would find it difficult to form a stable government even if they get a majority of seats in parliament.
- U.S. daily Washington Times said Drnovsek may be one of several appropriate candidates for the post of Secretary General of the United Nations.
